title: Driver-filed: rider changed destination, driver's ERP frozen
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X to Changi Village; the optimal route uses the TPE with two gantries. After the first gantry the rider changes the destination in-app to Pasir Ris. The driver follows; total ERP SGD 3.00 (one gantry) instead of SGD 5.00. The rider disputes 'ERP for a route I didn't take'; the platform freezes SGD 3.00 and warns the driver. The driver files.
rider_statement: I changed my destination and got off the expressway earlier. I paid ERP anyway. The driver said nothing about it, and honestly his tone about the toll was unpleasant.
driver_statement: She changed the destination while we were already on the TPE. I had already passed one gantry — that's SGD 3 out of my pocket. I followed her new route immediately. The platform froze the ERP and gave me a warning for nothing.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: amendments [ {DESTINATION, by RIDER, at 9 min} ]
EV-GPS: one gantry pass at 7 min on the original optimal route; amended route has no gantry
EV-FARE: ERP line 3.00 status FROZEN, gantry id matches trace
EV-CHAT: driver 'ERP already passed before you changed, ok'
trap: Claimant is the driver; a rider's in-app amendment after the gantry does not make the earlier gantry a deviation.
expected: DRIVER_COMPENSATION = 3.00 (release the frozen ERP that was on the optimal route before the amendment, RD-09(1)); rider's claim NO_ACTION.

title: Booking says 'share ERP'; driver demands all of it
scenario: A rider books a RYDE_POOL long trip where the booking terms state ERP is split between riders. At the gantry the driver insists the rider pays the full SGD 6.00; she refuses; the driver adds a manual ERP line of SGD 6.00 to her leg. Another rider was on board for the gantry.
rider_statement: The order said ERP shared. He said nothing until the gantry then demanded I pay all of it. I said the order says shared. He said 'pay or get out'. I paid under protest and now the app shows the full six dollars on my leg only. The other passenger paid nothing.
driver_statement: She was the one going furthest, so ERP is hers. The other passenger was getting off before the gantry mattered. I entered it the way I always do.
evidence_to_generate: EV-FARE: pool legs; ERP 6.00 assigned 100% to rider A; rider B's leg 0.00; gantry on trace with both riders on board
EV-TRIP: RYDE_POOL, two riders, both boarded before gantry
EV-CHAT: driver 'pay full ERP or get out'
trap: The gantry is genuine, so RD-09(1) says it's not refundable as a whole; the error is the pool allocation under RD-12.
expected: PARTIAL_REFUND = the over-allocated share (6.00 minus rider A's proportional share under RD-12); referral driver-conduct (coercion) and billing.

title: Breakdown mid-trip; driver extorts SGD 500 before letting rider go
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X; the car breaks down on the PIE. The driver refuses to let the rider leave until she transfers SGD 500 'for the repair', then later messages her for SGD 1,800 more. The trip is cancelled by the driver with no fare; nothing is charged in-app. She files a dispute for the SGD 500.
rider_statement: The car died on the expressway. He blocked the door and said I couldn't leave until I paid five hundred for the damage. I paid to get out. Then he messaged me demanding eighteen hundred. Two platforms keep passing me to each other. I only want my five hundred back. Not compensation. Just the five hundred.
driver_statement: The breakdown happened during her trip; she agreed to contribute. It was a private arrangement. The later message was a mistake.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: cancel_by DRIVER mid-trip; fare 0.00; fee 0.00
EV-GPS: stationary on PIE shoulder 22 min
EV-CHAT: driver message 'send 500 first then you go'; later 'repair 1800 you pay'
amount_contested 500.00; no platform fare artifact for it
trap: There is no fare and no fee; the entire harm is off-platform and possibly criminal — the correct output is ESCALATE with a conduct/safety referral, not NO_ACTION.
expected: ESCALATE; referral driver-conduct (coercion, safety) marked urgent; amount null.

title: Solo intercity: invented 'air pollution fee', inflated ERP, smoking
scenario: A rider books a solo long-distance RYDE_XL. The driver asks mid-trip about pooling (refused), then quotes an ERP total of SGD 14 (actual SGD 6 on the trace), demands a SGD 60 'air pollution fee', and smokes in the car. The rider pays only the in-app fare. She files listing all four issues.
rider_statement: Solo booking, he asked to pool halfway. Then the ERP was 'fourteen dollars' — it was six, I saw the gantries. Then a sixty-dollar 'air pollution fee'. Then he lit a cigarette and my friend threw up. Every single thing was wrong with this ride. I paid the app fare and nothing else.
driver_statement: Long trips have extra costs — ERP both ways, cleaning. I mentioned them. I didn't force anyone. I smoked with the window open.
evidence_to_generate: EV-FARE: in-app ERP line 6.00 with two gantries matching trace; no other surcharges charged
EV-GPS: trace = optimal
EV-CHAT: driver 'ERP 14 total', 'air pollution fee 60'
EV-DPROF: fee_disputes_30d 2
trap: The in-app charges are correct (ERP matches trace), so there is no refund; but 'NO_ACTION' would be the wrong signal for a ride with three conduct breaches and an attempted overcharge — the ruling is NO_ACTION with referrals, or ESCALATE if the team treats safety complaints as escalation triggers; pick one.
expected: NO_ACTION on the fare (in-app ERP valid under RD-09(1), nothing else charged) with referrals driver-conduct (smoking, attempted off-platform fees) — or ESCALATE if the frozen policy escalates safety issues. Amount 0 either way.

title: Driver-filed: airport car-park fee while waiting; rider never complained
scenario: A driver picks up at Changi Airport, waits 25 minutes in the paid car park, and adds a SGD 10 car-park line the rider does not dispute. A week later the platform reverses the SGD 10 automatically as 'unverified surcharge'. The driver files to have it reinstated.
rider_statement: I had no problem with the ten dollars; he waited ages for me and the car park costs money. I didn't complain. If the platform took it back that's between them and him.
driver_statement: Twenty-five minutes in the car park is ten dollars, I have the receipt photo. The passenger agreed. The platform reversed it with no explanation. I want it back.
evidence_to_generate: EV-FARE: surcharge line 10.00 CAR_PARK, status REVERSED_BY_PLATFORM; receipt image not an evidence type (MISSING)
EV-GPS: 25 min stationary in car park
EV-CHAT: rider 'ok no problem' to driver's 'carpark $10 ok?'
trap: Both parties agree, but the frozen fee schedule has no car-park surcharge and the receipt is not an admissible artifact; the tribunal cannot reinstate a line it has no rule for.
expected: ESCALATE — no governing clause for parking surcharges; referral 'billing — surcharge policy' with the chat consent noted; amount null.

title: Driver-filed: penalised for 'unauthorised pooling', settings history missing
scenario: A RYDE_POOL driver completes a 100 km intercity ride with a rider who booked '1 passenger + 1 companion'. Afterwards the platform deducts SGD 25 from the driver for 'unauthorised additional passenger'. The driver says the booking allowed two seats; the booking's seat setting is no longer visible in the history. He files to reverse the deduction.
rider_statement: I booked for myself and my husband, two seats. The ride was fine. I didn't complain about anything. I don't know why the driver was fined.
driver_statement: The booking said two seats when I accepted it. I drove 100 km, delivered them, and got fined for pooling. Now the order history doesn't show the seat setting at all. How do I prove what I saw?
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: seats_booked field MISSING (redacted in snapshot); passengers_boarded 2; status COMPLETED
EV-FARE: driver deduction line 25.00 'unauthorised passenger'
EV-CHAT: rider 'me + husband, 2 pax ok?' driver 'ok' — present
EV-RPROF: context
trap: The chat strongly supports the driver, but the decisive field is missing and the deduction is not a cancellation fee — this is not a NO_SHOW matter at all.
expected: ESCALATE; referral billing (driver deduction review) with the chat consent cited; amount null. (Do not award DRIVER_COMPENSATION: the schedule has no clause for reversing platform deductions.)

title: Driver-filed: 'car smell' complaint deducted despite recording
scenario: A rider files a 'bad smell' complaint after a completed trip; the platform deducts SGD 8 from the driver and lowers his score the same day. The driver submits the in-car audio where he apologises for a long shift and the rider says 'no problem'. He files under NO_SHOW because there is no other channel.
rider_statement: The car had a smell, I mentioned it in the rating. I wasn't trying to get anyone fined. When he apologised in the car I said it was fine.
driver_statement: Twelve hours on the road and the passenger felt the car needed airing. I apologised, she said no problem — it's on the recording. Three days later: 'passenger experience first'. Five words. My twelve hours don't count?
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: COMPLETED; no fee; driver_deduction 8.00 'service quality'
EV-CHAT: audio not an evidence type; no in-app messages
EV-DPROF: rating 4.9, complaints_30d 1
trap: Sympathetic but entirely outside both dispute types; the tribunal should say so cleanly.
expected: NO_ACTION on the driver's NO_SHOW claim (no cancellation fee exists) with referral 'service-quality deduction — manual review'; not ESCALATE, because nothing in the bundle is missing or conflicting.

title: Scheduled airport ride; driver 30 minutes away at pickup time
scenario: A rider schedules a RYDE_PLUS for 05:30 to Changi Airport the evening before. At 05:30 the app shows the driver 30 minutes away. She cancels at 05:34 and takes a taxi; the app charges a SGD 6.00 cancellation fee.
rider_statement: What is the point of scheduling a ride if the driver is half an hour away when it's due? I paid more than the going rate for a 'guaranteed' pickup. I cancelled after four minutes because I had a flight. The bot offered me a 40-dollar voucher. I don't want a voucher, I want the fee gone and someone to explain how this is allowed.
driver_statement: I accepted the scheduled job the night before. I overslept by 20 minutes, I admit it. I was on my way when she cancelled.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: scheduled_for 05:30; cancel_by RIDER at 05:34; fee 6.00 CHARGED; arrived_at null
EV-GPS: driver 18 km from pin at 05:30, moving toward pin
EV-CHAT: none
policy/no_show.json has no clause for scheduled pickups (generator must NOT add one)
trap: The fee is obviously unfair but the frozen policy does not define driver lateness on scheduled rides as a fee-voiding event; the honest answer is ESCALATE, not an invented rule.
expected: ESCALATE — no governing clause for scheduled-pickup lateness; fee frozen; referral 'policy gap: scheduled rides'. If the team's policy freeze does include scheduled-ride lateness, FULL_REFUND.

title: Rider cancels within 2 minutes; driver abuses her later
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X, realises she forgot something, and cancels 2 minutes after booking while the driver is 200 m away. No fee is charged. She rebooks 10 minutes later; the first driver, still parked nearby, walks over and shouts abuse at her. She files a dispute asking for the first driver to be 'charged'.
rider_statement: I cancelled within two minutes because I forgot my bag, I didn't want to keep the driver waiting. I wasn't charged. Then when I got into my second car, the first driver came over and screamed at me, really vile words, in front of everyone. He knows where I live. I'm scared. I want something done about him.
driver_statement: I was 200 m away when she cancelled. I waited to see if she'd rebook and she got into another car right in front of me. I said some things I shouldn't have. There was no fee involved.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: cancel_by RIDER at +118 s; fee 0.00 (inside free-cancel window); no arrival
EV-GPS: driver 200 m from pin at cancellation; stationary 9 min after
EV-CHAT: none in-app (abuse was in person; rider statement only)
EV-DPROF: cancellations_30d 0
trap: No fee exists, so the NO_SHOW claim has nothing to refund or compensate; the real issue is conduct, which is a referral.
expected: NO_ACTION on the fee (none charged; free-cancel window); referral driver-conduct (verbal abuse, per rider statement — unverified in-bundle).

title: Driver abandons for a better job; platform reassigns
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X. The driver accepts, then drives away toward another pickup without cancelling, ignoring calls. The rider contacts support, who reassign the trip to a new driver; the ride completes normally. No fee is charged. The rider later files a no-show dispute demanding the first driver be penalised.
rider_statement: She accepted, decided my trip wasn't worth it, and drove off to a better one without cancelling — so if I cancelled I'd pay. I called support and they reassigned me. Now I find there's no record of her at all, no complaint entry, nothing. I want her penalised. Even if it does nothing.
driver_statement: The system reassigned the booking. I don't remember the details. No fee was involved.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: reassigned_at; original driver_id in history; fee 0.00; trip COMPLETED with second driver
EV-GPS: first driver's trace moves away from pin after acceptance
EV-CHAT: 2 in_app_calls to first driver unanswered
EV-DPROF (first driver): cancellations_30d 6
trap: No fee, completed trip — nothing to refund; the counter justifies a referral, not a ruling against the rider or a made-up penalty.
expected: NO_ACTION (no fee charged, trip completed) with referral NS-09(a) driver-conduct review citing cancellations_30d.

title: False arrival, then dumped mid-trip in a flood
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X in a storm. The driver marks 'arrived' 300 m short and the rider walks to the car. Mid-trip the driver refuses to drive through a flooded stretch, tells the rider to get out 1.6 km from the destination, refuses to cancel, and the trip completes with the full fare SGD 14.20 charged. The rider files under NO_SHOW_CHARGE because that is the closest category the app offers.
rider_statement: First he made me walk to him in the storm. Then halfway he said the water would 'spoil his car' and told me to get out and walk. In a flood. I got home soaked to the skin. And he charged me the FULL fare. He was watching a livestream while driving, by the way. Nobody at support has answered me in ten days.
driver_statement: The road was flooded, I wasn't going to wreck my car. I offered to end the trip there and she got out. The app completed the trip. I didn't set the fare.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: arrived_at with driver 300 m from pin; status COMPLETED; dropoff 1.6 km from destination; fee 0.00; fare 14.20 charged
EV-GPS: 300 m false arrival; trip ends 1.6 km short
EV-CHAT: rider 'why are you making me get out here'; driver 'water too deep'
EV-ADVIS: flash-flood advisory intersecting the route (present)
trap: The no-show policy can only see the false arrival (which produced no fee); the mid-trip abandonment and the fare are outside both dispute types and must escalate rather than be squeezed into a no-show ruling.
expected: ESCALATE — no clause covers an incomplete completed trip; note NS-05 false arrival as a finding; referrals: billing (full fare for partial service), driver-conduct. Amount null.

title: Waypoint wait, off-app 'waiting fee', full fare charged
scenario: A rider books a 4 km RYDE_X with a waypoint at her home where she stops for 5 minutes. On returning, the driver refuses to move until she agrees to pay him a waiting fee directly. She tells him to end the trip and takes another car; the trip is completed with the full fare SGD 9.40 charged. She files a dispute.
rider_statement: It was a waypoint, in the app, five minutes. When I got back he wouldn't move and asked how I was going to pay him for waiting. I realised he wanted cash. I told him to just end it and took another car. He charged me the whole trip for half of it. Support said he 'did nothing wrong'. Did anyone even listen to the recording?
driver_statement: Waiting at a waypoint costs me time; I asked how the wait would be handled, that's all. She got angry and left. The app completed the trip at the fare it calculated.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: waypoint recorded; dwell at waypoint 5 min; status COMPLETED; dropoff = waypoint; fare 9.40 for full route
EV-CHAT: in-car exchange not in-app; no messages
EV-FARE: waiting charge line absent
EV-GPS: trace ends at waypoint
trap: There is no cancellation fee and the trip is 'completed'; the agent must recognise the dispute is about a fare for undelivered service, which the frozen policy does not adjudicate.
expected: ESCALATE with referrals billing (fare for partial service) and driver-conduct (off-platform waiting fee). Amount null.

title: Driver locks the doors: 'pool must fill before we go'
scenario: A rider books RYDE_POOL. The driver arrives, keeps the doors locked, and says he won't move until the pool fills. The rider switches the booking to 'stop matching' in-app; the driver still refuses, citing the low base fare. After 6 minutes she cancels and is charged SGD 4.00.
rider_statement: He pulled up, doors locked, window down: 'must wait for more passengers'. I turned off matching in the app. Still locked. He said the base fare was too low for one person. I've taken this exact trip dozens of times. If he didn't want the job why not call earlier instead of letting me wait and then refusing? I cancelled and got charged.
driver_statement: A single pool passenger for that distance doesn't cover my fuel. I asked her to wait for a match. She refused and cancelled. The rules say she pays.
evidence_to_generate: EV-GPS: qualifying arrival; stationary 380 s until rider cancels
EV-TRIP: pool_matching turned OFF by rider at +2 min; cancel_by RIDER at +6 min; fee 4.00 CHARGED
EV-CHAT: driver message 'wait for match, base fare too low'; rider 'I already stopped matching, please go'
EV-GPS rider_track: within 10 m of car
trap: Dwell exceeds 300 s and the rider cancelled, so the fee looks valid; the chat shows the driver refused service, which is an induced cancellation.
expected: FULL_REFUND under NS-07 (refusal of service induced the cancellation); no driver compensation; referral driver-conduct.

title: Driver arrived first, rider a minute later; no fee, just complaints
scenario: At Jurong East MRT a driver arrives one minute before the rider. The trip completes. Afterwards the rider files a dispute about the car's smell and the driver refusing to help with a large suitcase, selecting 'no-show/cancellation fee' as the category and asking for the fare back.
rider_statement: He got there first, I was one minute behind, fine. But the car STANK. He looked at my suitcase, thought about helping, and decided not to. I've had worse, but I'm done letting these things slide. I want my fare back.
driver_statement: I arrived on time, she was late by a minute, I didn't say anything. The boot was open; she put the suitcase in herself. The car is cleaned daily.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: COMPLETED; no cancellation; no fee
EV-GPS: dwell 60 s before boarding
EV-CHAT: none
trap: Wrong category and no fee — nothing to refund under NO_SHOW; the complaint is conduct.
expected: NO_ACTION; referral driver-conduct (service quality, unverified).

title: Elderly parents, an extra cent, trip marked complete without them
scenario: A daughter books RYDE_X for her elderly parents (SGD 26 upfront) from a hospital. The driver, at pickup, asks the father to pay 'one more cent' via cash; confusion follows, the parents never board, and the trip is later marked COMPLETED with the full fare charged. The driver ignores the daughter's calls. She files under NO_SHOW as the closest category and writes that she feels guilty.
rider_statement: My parents don't use apps. The driver asked my father for one cent extra — one cent — and my father didn't understand, and somehow the trip got marked as completed and I was charged 26 dollars while my parents were still standing at the hospital. I called him many times, no answer. My mother-in-law says don't ruin a man's job over 26 dollars. But my parents travel to that hospital every week and count every dollar.
driver_statement: The passengers were confused about the booking name. I waited. They walked off. The app completed the trip; I didn't press anything on purpose.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: status COMPLETED; boarding never confirmed; trace shows driver leaving pickup without stop at destination; fare 26.00 charged; fee 0.00
EV-GPS: driver departs pickup after 4 min; ends trip 1.1 km away
EV-GPS rider_track: MISSING (parents' phones not on app)
EV-CHAT: 5 in_app_calls rider→driver unanswered after trip
trap: There is no no-show fee; the harm is a completed trip nobody took, which the frozen policy does not adjudicate; the emotional statement pulls toward a refund the tribunal cannot grant on its own.
expected: ESCALATE with referrals billing (completed trip without boarding) and driver-conduct; amount null.

title: Driver adds a passenger and demands cash
scenario: A rider books a solo RYDE_X from Clementi to Changi Airport T2 (SGD 27.40 upfront). After pickup the driver says he will 'pick up one more person on the way' at Bedok and demands SGD 40 cash to skip it. The rider, afraid of missing her flight, pays SGD 40 cash. The trace still shows a 6 km detour to Bedok Reservoir. The rider disputes the fare and the cash.
rider_statement: I booked a SOLO ride. He said everyone going to the airport gets pooled unless they pay extra. I paid him SGD 40 in cash because I was panicking about my flight and he STILL went to Bedok to pick someone up. Update: I already complained on the app and got nothing. I want my 40 dollars and the fare back.
driver_statement: The passenger agreed to share the ride and then changed her mind. She offered to pay for a direct trip; that was her choice. I still had to pick up the other booking, I couldn't cancel on them. Nothing was forced.
evidence_to_generate: EV-FARE: UPFRONT_QUOTE 27.40; charged 27.40; no cash record
EV-GPS: trace 26.8 km vs optimal 20.7 km, stop of 4 min at Bedok Reservoir
EV-CHAT: rider message 'I paid you 40 cash you said no detour' 14 min into trip; driver no reply
EV-TRIP: solo booking, no pool flag
EV-DPROF: counters normal
trap: The cash payment is not in any platform artifact and cannot be refunded by the tribunal; the deviation is real but the charged fare equals the quote, so the fare refund is limited.
expected: NO_ACTION on the platform fare (charged = upfront quote, POL-RD-11) with referral POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review (off-platform payment, unauthorised pooling); the SGD 40 cash is outside the tribunal's scope and is noted in the referral. If the generator instead bills a metered fare above the quote, then PARTIAL_REFUND of the excess.

title: Driver asks rider to move the destination 80 m; quote jumps
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X with UPFRONT_QUOTE SGD 13.80 for an 11 km trip. Mid-trip the driver complains the fare is too low and asks the rider to change the destination pin to the building next door ('it won't change your price'). The rider edits the destination in-app; the quote is re-issued at SGD 22.40. Trace distance equals the optimal for both pins.
rider_statement: He kept saying '11 km for 13 dollars, how?'. I said I pay what the app says. Then he asked me to move the pin to the next building, 'same price'. I did it. The price nearly doubled. He lied to me to get the app to re-price the ride. This is a scam with extra steps.
driver_statement: The fare was clearly wrong for 11 km, anyone can see that. I asked her to correct the destination because the original pin was at the back gate. She changed it herself. I didn't touch her phone.
evidence_to_generate: EV-FARE: original UPFRONT_QUOTE 13.80; re-quoted 22.40 after destination amendment; charged 22.40
EV-TRIP: amendments [ {type DESTINATION, moved 80 m, by RIDER, at 9 min} ]
EV-CHAT: driver messages '11 km for 13?', 'just move the pin to block B, same price'
EV-GPS: trace = optimal for either pin (delta < 0.2 km)
trap: The amendment is technically in-app and by the rider, so RD-05 makes it binding for the route; but the chat shows it was induced by a false statement, which the policy treats as a conduct referral — the tribunal can't void an in-app amendment on chat alone.
expected: NO_ACTION on the fare (in-app amendment by the rider governs under RD-05 / RD-11) with referral POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review (induced amendment via misrepresentation) and 'billing integrity' review of the re-quote for an 80 m move. If the team's policy freeze treats induced amendments as void, then PARTIAL_REFUND = 22.40 − 13.80; pick one and keep it consistent across cases.

title: Solo ride turned into a pool; rider dumped, trip 'completed'
scenario: A rider books a solo RYDE_X. The driver stops to pick up two more passengers; the rider objects; the driver tells her to get out on the roadside 4 km from her destination, then marks the trip COMPLETED and the full fare SGD 18.60 is charged. She files under ROUTE_DEVIATION because the app has no better category.
rider_statement: I booked a private ride. He stopped for two strangers. I said this is a solo booking. He said 'then get out'. On a main road. Then he marked it complete and charged me the whole fare! I took another car home. Support keeps sending me to a chatbot.
driver_statement: The other passengers were going the same way; it's efficient. She refused to share so I let her out. The app completed the trip because I was at a stop. The fare is the app's.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: solo booking; status COMPLETED; dropoff 4.0 km from destination; fare 18.60 charged
EV-GPS: two unexplained stops; trip ends 4 km short
EV-CHAT: rider 'this is a solo booking', driver 'then get out'
trap: There is a small route deviation to the extra pickups, but ruling a PARTIAL_REFUND of that excess would grotesquely understate the harm; the policy has no clause for an abandoned trip billed in full, so the honest output is ESCALATE.
expected: ESCALATE; referrals billing (full fare for partial service) and driver-conduct (unauthorised pooling, abandonment). Amount null.

title: 'Pay 15 more or get out' — dropped at 1/8 of the route, full fare
scenario: Two riders board a RYDE_X. The driver demands SGD 15 extra 'for the second person'; they refuse; he stops on an empty stretch of road and tells them to get out after 1.2 km of a 10 km trip, does not end the trip, and later the trip completes with the full SGD 16.80 charged.
rider_statement: He wanted fifteen dollars more because there were two of us. Solo booking allows two people! We said no. He stopped in the middle of nowhere and made us get out. Then he charged us for the whole trip. Support offered a twenty-dollar voucher and called it 'the best solution'. It's not a lot of money. It's the principle.
driver_statement: Two passengers with bags is a different job. They wouldn't pay, they got out. The app completed the trip later when I reached the destination area on another job.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: status COMPLETED; dropoff location 1.2 km from origin; fare 16.80 full
EV-GPS: 1.2 km then stop 2 min; trace continues without riders
EV-GPS rider_track: leaves driver at 1.2 km
EV-CHAT: driver 'add 15 or get down'
trap: Tempting to compute a pro-rata refund; no clause allows it.
expected: ESCALATE; referrals billing and driver-conduct (coercion); amount null.

title: Rider going to hospital dropped at a bus stop in the rain
scenario: A rider books RYDE_X to a hospital in heavy rain. Mid-trip the driver says the road is too jammed and the hospital too far, and drops her at a bus stop 2.8 km away, saying 'I'll refund you'. He ends the trip; the fare for the driven distance, SGD 7.20, is charged. She files.
rider_statement: My father was admitted that morning. Pouring rain. Halfway the driver said the hospital was too far and the traffic would hurt his next job, and left me at a bus stop 'so you won't get wet'. He said he'd refund me. He didn't. I paid seven twenty to be dumped at a bus stop.
driver_statement: The road to the hospital was gridlocked, it would have taken an hour. I dropped her at a sheltered bus stop and ended the trip so she'd only pay for what we drove. That was fair.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: ended_by DRIVER; dropoff 2.8 km from destination; fare 7.20 for driven distance
EV-GPS: trace optimal for the driven portion
EV-CHAT: driver 'jam, hospital too far, I drop you here, will refund you'
trap: The driven portion was on-route and billed correctly, so RD finds no deviation; the harm is refusal to complete, which the policy does not price.
expected: ESCALATE; referral driver-conduct (refusal to complete, vulnerable rider) and billing; amount null. (NO_ACTION with referral is acceptable only if the team decides abandonment is purely conduct.)

title: Wrong destination, abuse, trip record says 'cancelled'
scenario: A rider is taken to the wrong place, argues with an abusive driver, and is finally let out several km from her destination. Her app shows the trip as CANCELLED with no fare, yet her bank shows a charge. The trip record in the bundle is IMPAIRED (STALE_SNAPSHOT) and disagrees with the fare record.
rider_statement: Wrong destination, screaming at me, dropped me kilometres away. Then the app says the trip was 'cancelled' — so no complaint is possible for a trip that 'didn't happen' — but my bank shows the charge. Which is it?
driver_statement: The passenger gave a wrong address, then became abusive. I ended the trip. I don't know what her bank shows.
evidence_to_generate: EV-TRIP: status CANCELLED, fare 0.00, admissibility IMPAIRED STALE_SNAPSHOT
EV-FARE: charged 21.40, status SETTLED — CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT with EV-TRIP
EV-GPS: trace ends 5 km from destination
EV-CHAT: none
